title: Put half of the six bolts in a cup
instruction: put half of the bolts in the cup
context: Counting out parts ('half of these', 'three of those') is routine in assembly and stores work, and counting is a known weak spot of vision-language-action models, which tend to move everything or a single item. The robot has to count the bolts and halve the number.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward is away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. (1) Bolts: six steel bolts, modelled as rods 1.6 cm across and 6 cm long, 95 g each, standing on end, loose, in a row 16 cm forward at 20, 12 and 4 cm left and 4, 12 and 20 cm right. (2) Cup: a blue open box, fixed, 13 x 13 cm inside, with 4 mm walls 5 cm tall on a 3 mm floor, centred 37 cm forward on the midline. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored once, after the episode ends. A bolt is in the cup if its centre is inside the cup's walls, below their tops. 1.0: exactly three bolts are in the cup, any three. 0.0 otherwise: fewer, more, or none.
reset_notes: Stand the bolts back in their row. The cup is fixed (tape or putty).
fidelity: Calibrated YAM station replica in Isaac Lab-Arena (Isaac Sim). The cup is a fixed rigid box; the bolts are rigid cylinders of the stated size and mass (no head or thread). Lighting and cameras follow the station calibration.
